summary:
Several well-known Dutch women are considering legal action after manipulated pornographic videos featuring their faces appeared on a website with 13 million monthly visitors. The victims include artists, TV presenters, Olympic athletes, former ministers, mayors, and members of the royal family. The platform advises uploaders to stay anonymous, likely to avoid prosecution, and pays more for high views. Outgoing justice minister Yesilgöz called the videos disgusting and urged victims to report them. Some managers confirmed reports have been filed or are being considered.

Deepfake pornography is illegal under Dutch revenge porn laws. After a report, prosecutors can try to shut down the site. Victims may also start a mass claim, complain to the data protection authority, or contact hosting companies. A previous case involved presenter Welmoed Sijtsma, whose deepfake maker received a 180-hour suspended community service sentence last November. Lawyers warn that more such videos will appear if the government does not act.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
